findings.message: Independently re-counted the three sentence-length fixes claimed in work/revision-notes.r10.md, using the same splitting rule validate-draft.ts uses (split on sentence-ending punctuation, count [A-Za-z'] tokens), not just trusting the notes. late-for-school 4th paragraph: 'Eli's library book had a map, and he was meant to show it in class.' = 15 words (was 17 with 'in it'). frog-helped 4th paragraph: 'She was waiting at the stairs, and she gave him a small, surprised smile.' = 14 words (was 17 with 'the start of'). home-too-soon 5th paragraph: 'He looked at his muddy shoes and thought of the marsh, the stairs and the hatch.' = 16 words exactly (was 17 with 'dark'), right at the brief's ceiling with zero room to spare. All three match the notes' own counts. I then scanned every sentence in all 52 passages (not just the three touched ones) with the same rule and found zero sentences over 16 words anywhere in story.r10.json, confirming reports/validation.r10.json's brief.warnings is now genuinely empty (it read '3 sentence(s) exceed the brief's 16-word limit' on r9) rather than trusting that field alone.

Diffed story.r9.json against story.r10.json directly (not just reading the notes) and confirmed only these 5 passages changed: late-for-school, frog-helped, home-too-soon, tower-hall, the-stairs, each by exactly the one sentence the notes describe, with no other text, choice, target, item, clue or flag touched anywhere in the document (JSON-equal elsewhere; only the story 'version' field differs at the top level). This matches the notes' explicit claim of scope.

Confirmed the fronted-subordinate-clause fix on the two carried-over hubs matches the model fix lantern-room and varro used in r9, which I re-read directly in story.r10.json (lantern-room's opening is still 'By one path or the other, Eli was here now.', unchanged since r9). tower-hall: 'However he had climbed those last steps, Eli reached the top at last.' -> 'By one path or another, Eli reached the top at last.' - no embedded subject+verb before the comma, same shape as lantern-room. the-stairs: 'Whatever Eli had just decided, he turned to climb the stairs.' -> 'Either way, Eli turned to climb the stairs.' - same fix. I independently re-derived the incoming-edge counts from story.r10.json's choice targets rather than trusting the notes: tower-hall has 7 incoming choices and the-stairs has 13, exactly matching the notes' claim that the reworded opening still signals a hub reached by many different preceding routes. The stacked 'Whatever'/'However' comprehension-load note from review-13-literacy.r9.json (carried over specifically for these two passages) is resolved by this revision; I did not find any remaining instance of the pattern on any passage.

The revision notes' verification claim ('No word-set target word (blend-words, closed-syllable-words, ing-words) was removed or added by these edits') is not fully accurate, and I caught this only by diffing reports/literacy.r9.json's perWord against reports/literacy.r10.json's directly rather than trusting the claim. tower-hall's old sentence 'However he had climbed those last steps, Eli reached the top at last.' contained 'steps', a plural match of the blend-words target word 'step' (the analyzer matches -s/-es forms per its documented method). Removing that sentence's wording dropped 'step' from 29 to 28 occurrences and the blend-words total from 105 to 104, and because tower-hall sits on the path to every ending, perEndingRoute for blend-words dropped by exactly 1 on all five routes (e.g. home-too-soon: 11 -> 10). This does not cause a failure: 104 still clears the floor of 10 by a wide margin, and 10 on home-too-soon still equals, not misses, its minimum, so word-set-minimums and word-sets-on-every-route both still report ok:true. But the home-too-soon route for blend-words is now at its exact floor (10/10) with zero margin, alongside ing-words on the same route, which was already at its exact floor (8/8) before this revision. Two of the three sets now have no slack left on the shortest route to home-too-soon. I recommend the revision notes be corrected (the claim as written is false for this one word), and that any future trim on tower-hall, the-stairs, or any other passage on the home-too-soon route avoid removing further blend-words or ing-words occurrences, since the next such edit could silently fail the minimum. closed-syllable-words and ing-words totals and every perEndingRoute value are otherwise unchanged between r9 and r10 (confirmed by the same diff), and no word-set word was added either.

Noting for future revisions: reports/literacy.r10.json's own 'sentence-length' automatedCheck reports against a 20-word threshold ('0 sentence(s) over 20 words'), not the brief's 16-word maxSentenceWords. That check alone would not have caught the three overages this revision fixed, and would not catch a future one either. The authoritative signal for the brief's own limit is reports/validation.r10.json's brief.warnings (now empty), which I reproduced independently with the same regex validate-draft.ts uses across the full 52-passage story, not just the three touched passages.

Limits of automated detection, restated for this revision: reports/literacy.r10.json and the analyzer behind it detect spelling patterns, not sound, and the word-set and sentence-length checks are deterministic token counts, not a judgement of decodability, naturalness or whether a specific child's program would call these patterns by the same name. conceptMismatches is empty for all three word sets and I spot-checked 'map' (closed syllable: single vowel between two consonants) and 'hop' (same) directly in the touched passages' surrounding text; both still carry the declared pattern. This review remains an AI pre-review recorded with reviewer.kind 'ai-agent' and is not the human literacy review the publication policy requires; it does not set literacy.review.status to 'passed'.

Skills practised: reading this story end to end, a child decodes in natural context short words with beginning consonant blends (step, stone, frog, plan, spin, trip, crab, drum), closed-syllable words (cat, map, net, lid, hop, mud, bus) and -ing words (running, jumping, hiding, climbing, glowing, ringing), with every set still clearing its stated minimum on the shortest route to every one of the 5 endings (blend-words 10-23, closed-syllable-words 18-27, ing-words 8-12 per reports/literacy.r10.json). Beyond phonics, the child follows cause and effect and sequence across the fall, the marsh, the stairs and the tower, tracks who is speaking across multi-character dialogue, makes inferences from clues (the small wet marks on the stairs, the shivering crab, Lira's doubt about the 'hero'), and meets new vocabulary in context with an 8-word glossary. Short average sentence length (8.1 words per reports/literacy.r10.json) and five distinct endings of different emotional weight suit the stated 10-to-13 age range without talking down to the reader.

shelfSummary.blurb: Eli follows a stray cat down a manhole into a fading magical land and must decide how to help its people, choosing his own path through a marsh, a stairway and a tower toward one of five endings. Along the way he reads and meets, again and again, words with beginning blends, short closed-syllable words and -ing words, in natural sentences rather than a word list.
